speaker: A
text: This little model looks magical in the sunset. Is the Taj Mahal really a palace?

speaker: C
text: It looks like one, but it is a mausoleum in Agra, beside the Yamuna River. There is a remarkable story behind it.

speaker: A
text: Tell me! I know people call it a monument to love. Who had it built?

speaker: C
text: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissioned it in memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Thousands of skilled artisans helped create it.

speaker: A
text: That explains the feeling. But what makes the building so special when you look closely?

speaker: C
text: Start with the white marble, the great dome, and the balanced arrangement of the minarets. Then notice the delicate floral stone inlay.

speaker: A
text: Flowers made from stone? We are surrounded by real daisies, and they captured that same beauty in marble.

speaker: C
text: Exactly. Craftspeople fitted carefully cut colored stones into the surface. The patterns reward a closer look.

speaker: A
text: It must have taken forever. When did they finish?

speaker: C
text: The main mausoleum was completed in sixteen forty-eight. Other parts of the complex were finished by sixteen fifty-three.

speaker: A
text: So the gardens matter just as much as the dome?

speaker: C
text: They shape the whole experience: ordered paths, water, greenery, and that first view of the monument. The setting makes the architecture even more graceful.

speaker: A
text: Now I want to visit Agra, take my time, and look for all those tiny flowers.

speaker: C
text: And treat the place with care. Great monuments are shared memories. The best journey leaves them beautiful for everyone.
